steps.say: A signal is one measurement of the market, worked out from price and volume on finished candles. | Each one answers a single question.
Most signals can be read on several timeframes, from fifteen minutes to weekly. | Hover any signal to see what it measures.
Trend signals ask: which way is the market going, and how firmly? | Traders use them to work with the main direction, rather than against it.
Momentum signals ask: how fast, and how stretched? | They help spot moves that have run hard, or are losing steam. A divergence is when price makes a new extreme, but momentum does not follow.
Regime asks: what kind of market is this? Trending or ranging, | and is volatility compressed or expanding? The same setup can mean different things in each.
Structure follows the swing highs and lows: | whether they are rising or falling, where price broke through, and the real price levels where swings have turned before.
Volume asks: is the crowd behind the move? | Rising prices on rising volume tell a different story from rising prices on thin volume.
Sentiment reads recent headlines about the asset, positive or negative. | Its history starts in November 2026 with the birth of Angstrom Signals.
On their own, signals are ingredients. | In Lattice you combine them into Groups, and Groups into Sets, so they are read together, the way a trader reads a chart.
Every signal describes what is happening now. None of them is a prediction, | which is why Lattice always shows a reading together with its reason.
